subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency qualification (hosted API vs current provider) - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - post-call recap

Thanks for the time today, Alex — good conversation. Quick recap from our discovery + the items we agreed to validate so we can qualify next steps: 

1) FinLytics perf targets (what we heard today):
- End-to-end p95 latency target: <= 300 ms
- End-to-end p99 latency target: <= 700 ms
- Baseline throughput: ~50 RPS sustained; burst capacity to ~200 RPS for short windows
- Typical concurrency per user: 2-6 concurrent streams
- Streaming requirement: token-streaming (partial responses) with low startup latency; we called out that partial-token latency should be <50 ms for interactive experience

2) Measurement/details we asked you to confirm:
- Where you currently measure (edge -> app -> provider -> app -> client) vs. provider-only internal metrics
- Typical prompt + response sizes (median prompt 180 tokens, expected response 120 tokens; worst-case sequence ~1,500 tokens)
- Model family you’re using with the current provider (you mentioned a finetuned LLM based on an open LLM)

3) Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Alex: share current provider perf logs (p95/p99 + raw traces) and an example prompt set — by EOD 8/13 (you mentioned you can export traces)
- Redwood: run an initial hosted vs. provider side-by-side perf test (synthetic harness with your prompt set + streaming enabled) and share a short SLO comparison + test plan — will target 8/20 for results
- Rishi/Marissa: schedule a 60m follow-up workshop to review test artifacts and any regressions (target week of 8/24)

Attached a short draft SLO comparison matrix to start (redwood-slo-comparison.xlsx). If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Thanks again — excited to dig in.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-slo-comparison.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: CTO - FinLytics <cto@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - post-call recap

Thanks, Marissa — appreciate the clear notes. A few quick answers from our side and I attached a small bundle of logs we exported from our current provider (provider-logs-aug.zip).

Current provider observed metrics (measured end-to-end from our app through to the provider and back):
- p95 = ~420 ms
- p99 = ~1,200 ms (we see a long tail under higher concurrency)
- Sustained throughput (our prod traffic) = ~60 RPS, with periodic spikes to ~180 RPS
- Concurrency: we see per-session concurrency up to 8 during heavy workflows which seems to trigger queueing on the provider side
- Streaming: provider supports chunked responses but startup latency is ~250-350 ms; token-chunk cadence is coarse which makes the UX feel laggy

Notes: our payloads are median prompt 160–200 tokens and average response ~140 tokens; we’re currently using a finetuned model hosted by the provider (not a base LLM). We can share a sanitized prompt set — I’ll drop that into the Drive link you sent once I have approval from the CTO.

Questions for Redwood: can you confirm what you’ll measure for the A/B? Is Redwood measuring pure provider-side latency or full end-to-end (including our app/network)? We prefer end-to-end to match real UX.

—
Alex Johnson
Head of Product
FinLytics
[Attachment: provider-logs-aug.zip (zip, 2.1MB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - post-call recap (measurement clarifications)

Short follow-up — two measurement clarifications so our test plan is apples-to-apples: 
1) Scope: we will run both (a) provider-measured latency (their internal telemetry) and (b) full end-to-end latency measured from FinLytics’ app edge -> Redwood hosted API -> back to the app edge (this will include network and TCP handshake times). We agree to prioritise end-to-end for the UX comparison.
2) Payloads & seq lengths: please confirm a small representative set (3–5 prompts) and a 95th/99th percentile length we should test to ensure we capture tail behavior (Alex: any chance you can share those by 8/13–14?).

Test proposal (quick):
- Synthetic harness that replays your prompt set with a distribution matching your traffic (burst windows)
- Concurrency targets: run tests at 50 RPS (baseline), 100 RPS, and 200 RPS (burst)
- Measure: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, time-to-first-byte (startup latency), per-token cadence for streaming, and achieved QPS under steady-state

If that plan looks good I’ll finalize the runbook and get infra scheduled. Proposed test date: 2026-08-20 (4–6 hour window) — ok for FinLytics?

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - test plan & next steps

Thanks Alex — and thanks Rishi for the test plan draft. Confirming next steps and owners so we have a clear schedule: 

1) FinLytics (Alex) by EOD 8/17: share sanitized prompt set (3–5 representative prompts), confirm 95/99 token lengths to test, and upload the provider logs to the shared Drive folder.
2) Redwood (Rishi + infra) by 8/20: run A/B perf tests (hosted API vs. FinLytics current provider) with:
   - Load targets: 50 / 100 / 200 RPS (sustained windows as Rishi outlined)
   - Measurements: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, time-to-first-byte (startup), per-token streaming cadence, and achieved throughput
   - Target SLOs for the hosted run we’ll try to meet: p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 600 ms (end-to-end) — we’ll report actuals and any caveats (region, model variant, quantization)
3) Workshop: schedule a 60m review for week of 8/24 to go over results and recommend config changes (batching/quantization/routing)

Attached the finalized short test plan for your review (redwood-slo-test-plan.pdf). I’ll also upload the raw test scripts and a short README to the Drive link once the prompt set is in place.

If FinLytics is aligned, I’ll lock the 8/20 test window and send a calendar invite for the 8/24 workshop.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
